name: Oligopeptide-34

lead: Oligopeptide-34 is a cosmetic peptide used in brightening products. People use it to help even out skin tone and fade the appearance of pigmented spots.
It is found in professional and retail serums aimed at hyperpigmentation.

paras: It is described as reducing tyrosinase activity and melanin synthesis in melanocytes and limiting melanosome transfer to skin cells.
It is a topical cosmetic ingredient. Reported efficacy figures come from company-run tests, and no independent human trials were found.

chain: Reduces tyrosinase activity and melanosome transfer
angle.text: Applied topically in brightening serums, Oligopeptide-34 is used to fade the appearance of pigmented spots and even out complexion.

lead: Oligopeptide-34 is a synthetic 13-amino-acid peptide used in skin-brightening cosmetics. People use serums containing it to help fade the look of dark spots and even out skin tone.[1]

It is described as acting on pigment cells: it reduces melanin synthesis and tyrosinase activity in melanocytes and lowers the transfer of melanosomes (packets of melanin) to surrounding keratinocytes.[1] The International Dermal Institute says it was developed with an Asian biopharmaceutical company specialising in growth-factor-mimicking peptides.[1]
Published information consists largely of supplier and brand-reported tests; no independent peer-reviewed human trial of the ingredient was found.
infobox: Reduces melanin synthesis and melanosome transfer

paras: Oligopeptide-34 is formulated into topical brightening products intended to address uneven tone and pigmented spots.[1]
Per the International Dermal Institute, the peptide reduces melanin synthesis and tyrosinase activity in melanocytes and reduces the transfer of melanosomes to keratinocytes.[1]

No independent published clinical studies found. The International Dermal Institute reports company-conducted results: in tests on human melanocytes stimulated with MSH, melanin dropped by about 33 percent and tyrosinase activity by 65 percent; in a comparison, pigmentation fell 47 percent versus 27 percent for vitamin C and 40 percent for arbutin.[1] It also reports a twice-daily study of 22 Asian participants showing a statistically significant brightening effect on pigmented spots, with 84 percent of panelists rating performance good or very good after eight weeks.[1]
